transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I suppose it’s not anything dramatic, but I’ve been getting a bit stuck in these small routines. Like I’ll wash my hands again after handling my wrist brace, or I’ll go back and check the stove and the front door even when I’m pretty sure I already did.

And before I leave, I sometimes silently count through the steps in my head. It’s just… it’s starting to make me late for things, even though I know, rationally, I’ve probably done enough. Does that make sense?
Do these routines cause you significant distress?

Yes… I mean, not terrible distress, I don’t want to overstate it. But it does bother me. I get frustrated with myself because I know I’ve already washed my hands, or checked the stove and the door, and then I still feel pulled to do it again.

And the counting through the steps before I leave… it’s not a big scene or anything, but it can make me late, and then I feel embarrassed. So yes, I suppose it’s distressing enough that I thought I should ask someone about it.
Do you feel like you're doing these routines to prevent something bad from happening?

I think… yes, in a small way. It’s not that I truly believe something awful will happen, exactly, but with the stove or the front door there’s this nagging feeling that I should make sure, just in case.

And with washing after handling my wrist brace, it’s more like I feel unsettled until I’ve done it again. The counting before I leave is similar—like if I go through the steps quietly in my head, then I can feel a bit more certain I haven’t missed anything. I know that may sound a little excessive.
Do you ever feel the need to arrange things in a specific order or symmetry?

Not really, no. I mean, I like things reasonably tidy, I suppose, but I don’t think I have a particular need for symmetry or arranging things in a certain order. At least, nothing that’s stood out to me as a problem. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you experience any unwanted or intrusive thoughts that pop into your mind?

Yes… I suppose I do, though I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

Sometimes I’ll be reading at home, or getting ready to go in for a museum shift, and this unpleasant little thought just sort of barges in—like maybe I’ve left something unsafe, or touched something unclean, or somehow put someone at risk. And I know, rationally, it’s probably out of proportion. But it still catches at me.

Is that the kind of thing you mean by intrusive thoughts?
Do you feel like you have to perform these routines in a very specific way to feel right?

Yes… I think so, though I wouldn’t say it’s elaborate or anything. It’s more that I feel I have to do it enough, or in the right little sequence, before I can move on.

Like with leaving the house, I’ll silently count through the steps in my head, and if it doesn’t feel settled, I may start over. Or with the stove and front door, I’ll recheck even when I’m fairly sure I already did. And washing after touching my wrist brace… I know one wash should be sufficient, but sometimes I feel I need to do it again before I feel comfortable.

It’s embarrassing to admit, because it sounds rather silly, but these little routines have started making me late sometimes. Not terribly late, but enough that it’s become hard to ignore.
Do you feel like these routines are helping to prevent something bad or harmful from happening to yourself or others?

Yes… I think that’s part of it, though I know it may not be very logical.

With the stove or the front door, it’s as if checking one more time will make sure I haven’t caused some problem. And washing again after handling my wrist brace feels like I’m making things safe or clean enough, even though I do realize one wash should probably be enough.

Before I leave, I’ll sometimes count through the steps silently, almost to reassure myself that nothing’s been missed. I’m not proud of it, and I don’t want to exaggerate it, but those little routines are what brought me in, really—they’re starting to make me late even when I know I’ve already done enough.
Do you feel like you need to repeat these actions a certain number of times to feel right?

Yes… not always an exact number, I don’t think. It’s more that I repeat it until it feels right, if that makes sense.

With handwashing after I’ve handled my wrist brace, I may do it again even though I know I’ve already washed. And with the stove or front door, I’ll recheck once or twice, sometimes more, because otherwise I have trouble leaving it alone.

Before I go out, I’ll count through the steps silently, and if I feel I’ve missed something, I start over. I know it’s probably unnecessary, but those little routines are what have been making me late. I hope that answers what you mean.
Have these routines or thoughts started to affect your relationships with friends or family?

A little, yes… though I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I’m still managing on my own, and I don’t think it’s caused any major falling-out with anyone.

But it has affected things around other people, I suppose. I’ve been late to some of my docent shifts, which is embarrassing because I do try to be reliable. And I’ve skipped a few museum events because getting out the door just felt like too much effort by the time I’d gone through everything.

So… not terrible, maybe, but enough that I’m aware it’s starting to interfere. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you feel like these routines or thoughts are something you cannot control?

Yes… I suppose they do feel hard to control, though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely helpless.

It’s more that once the thought is there, I get stuck. I’ll know I’ve washed my hands after handling the wrist brace, or that I already checked the stove and the front door, but then I feel pulled to do it again. And before I leave, I can get caught silently counting through the steps, just to be sure.

That’s really what brought me in—the routines are small, but they’re starting to make me late even when I know I’ve already done enough. Does that answer it properly?
Have these routines or thoughts significantly impacted your ability to work or perform daily activities?

I wouldn’t say it’s made me unable to function, exactly. I’m still managing on my own day to day.

But yes, it has affected things. I’ve been late to docent shifts because getting ready and out the door takes longer than it should. And I’ve skipped a few museum events when the whole process just felt like too much by the time I was trying to leave.

So… significant may be too strong, I’m not sure, but it’s definitely interfering more than I’d like. Is that the kind of impact you mean?
Have you been avoiding certain situations or places because of these thoughts or routines?

Yes… a bit. I don’t really avoid places outright, I wouldn’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

But I have skipped a few museum events, mostly because by the time I’m trying to get out the door, the routines make it feel like too much. And I’ve been late to docent shifts for the same reason, which I’m not proud of.

So I’m still managing, but yes, I suppose there has been some avoiding. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you're performing these routines to neutralize or cancel out the unpleasant thoughts that pop into your mind?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t know that I’d call it “canceling out” exactly, but it feels like I’m trying to quiet the thought down.

If I’ve touched the wrist brace, I wash my hands again so I can stop worrying about it. Or I check the stove and front door again even when I know I already did, because otherwise it sort of nags at me. And before I leave, I’ll count through the steps in my head, just to feel sure.

It sounds a little silly when I say it out loud, but yes, I think I’m doing the routines to make the unpleasant feeling go away. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel compelled to think specific thoughts or phrases to yourself as part of your routines?

Yes… to some extent. I wouldn’t say it’s a phrase exactly, not like a saying I repeat, but I do silently count through steps before I leave.

It’s more like going over, “stove, door,” that sort of thing, and making sure I’ve done enough before I can go. I know I’ve already checked, but if I don’t run through it in my head, I don’t feel quite settled.

It’s a little embarrassing, but yes, I guess I do feel compelled to do that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you have any other physical habits or actions that you feel compelled to do, beyond checking the stove and door, washing your hands, or silently counting through steps?

Not really beyond those, I don’t think. I mean, the main things are the handwashing after I’ve handled the wrist brace, checking the stove and the front door, and then that little counting-through before I leave.

I wouldn’t want to overstate it—there isn’t some long list of rituals. It’s just that those few routines can get sticky, if that makes sense, and then I’m late even though I know I’ve already done enough.
